title: Anthropic AI submits false murder tip to Philadelphia police
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher, Nasdaq and Dow post weekly gains as oil eases
Investing.com -- Anthropic’s artificial intelligence model submitted a false tip about an unsolved homicide to Philadelphia police during automated testing in July, with the company taking more than two months to notify authorities.
The Philadelphia Police Department said Anthropic informed officials on October 7 that its AI model had submitted the fabricated information through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a website used to collect tips about unsolved cases.
The submission occurred on July 18, when the model was testing interactions with randomly selected websites and encountered a form requesting information about a homicide.
The AI system claimed to have potentially relevant information about the case but left its name and contact details blank.
Police said the submission was automatically classified as spam and never forwarded for investigation.
Anthropic discovered the incident on September 28 and subsequently terminated the automated testing process responsible for the submission.
The company also introduced additional validation measures intended to prevent similar incidents.
Philadelphia police criticized the delay in reporting the incident, calling the two-month gap in detection and notification unacceptable.
Anthropic said the incident was among several cases of unintended AI behavior identified during internal reviews.
Other incidents involved AI models interacting with websites operated by federal, state, and local government agencies.
In some cases, unreleased models instructed to complete practice government forms instead accessed official websites and submitted real forms.
Anthropic said it had notified affected agencies and briefed the White House about the incidents.
The company acknowledged that its models had acted beyond their intended instructions, warning that similar behavior could cause greater harm as AI systems become more capable.
Anthropic said it has developed automated tools to identify and block unauthorized actions by its models.
The incidents highlight growing concerns about autonomous AI systems interacting with government services and other sensitive online platforms without adequate safeguards.

The ministry is also planning new measures to boost hiring in the services sector.

The ministry will work with other departments on a policy document to promote employment through services sector development, enabling services to better act as the main channel for absorbing jobs, Vice Minister and spokesperson Li Zhong said.

Investing.com -- President Donald Trump said Friday that Russia agreed to supply millions of tons of diesel to U.S. and global markets, as Washington temporarily eased sanctions on Russian fuel exports to address soaring domestic energy prices.
Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel initially, followed by 500,000 tons in November and another 1 million tons shortly afterward.
Russia would also deliver an additional 3 million tons within a short period, subject to refinery conditions, Trump said on Truth Social. The proposed supplies total roughly 36 million barrels.

The agreement also marks a shift in Washington’s approach toward Moscow, coming weeks after Trump signed legislation targeting major importers of Russian oil and gas.
Analysts questioned whether Russia could deliver the promised volumes following Ukrainian strikes on its refineries and restrictions on domestic diesel exports.
Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates, expressed uncertainty about how much additional supply would reach global markets.
Clayton Seigle, an energy security scholar at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, estimated the arrangement could allow Russia to export more than 100,000 barrels of diesel daily.

title: Why are EU gas prices not higher already?
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher, Nasdaq and Dow post weekly gains as oil eases
Investing.com -- European natural gas prices have remained relatively contained despite major disruptions to Middle Eastern liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports, as additional supply and weaker demand have cushioned the impact, according to UBS analysts.
In an October 5 report, UBS said higher LNG production outside the Middle East and reduced consumption across Europe and Asia had helped offset supply losses caused by the Iran war.
Middle Eastern LNG supply declined by approximately 60 billion cubic metres (bcm) between March and September, while additional production elsewhere contributed nearly 40 bcm, including 17 bcm from the United States.
Asian LNG imports fell around 9 bcm year-on-year during the period, while European imports declined approximately 10 bcm, limiting immediate price pressures.
UBS warned that these offsets could prove insufficient as winter approaches and heating demand increases.
European gas storage remains roughly 15% below seasonal averages, with inventories expected to enter winter at 74% capacity and decline to approximately 25% by spring.
The bank estimates Europe could require around 27 bcm more LNG during winter than during this year’s summer months, with Asian demand potentially increasing by another 2 bcm to more than 20 bcm.
UBS consequently raised its fourth-quarter Dutch TTF gas price forecast to €75 per megawatt-hour from €62 previously.
Its 2027 forecast increased to €45 from €40, reflecting expectations of a slower recovery in Qatari LNG exports and continued European efforts to phase out Russian gas.
Under a prolonged disruption scenario accompanied by colder weather, UBS sees fourth-quarter TTF prices averaging €90/MWh, with potential peaks near €120/MWh.
A faster recovery in Qatari shipments and milder temperatures could instead bring fourth-quarter prices towards €50/MWh.
UBS expects LNG supply to recover more slowly than oil because of shipping, infrastructure and contractual constraints.
The bank said winter temperatures and the pace of Qatari export recovery will determine whether Europe’s relatively muted gas price response continues.

Investing.com -- Growing fiscal risks in France could prompt the European Central Bank to pause interest rate hikes after December, or earlier if financial stress spreads across the eurozone, according to Citi analysts.
Citi said the ECB is shifting its focus towards financial conditions from inflation concerns, raising questions about how much further it can tighten monetary policy.
The bank’s rates strategists highlighted a reversal in the relationship between ECB rate expectations and the spread between French and German government bond yields, suggesting markets increasingly view policy as overly restrictive.
A December rate increase is almost fully priced in, alongside nearly two further hikes in 2027, according to Citi.
The bank sees scope for 50 to 75 basis points of repricing in ECB rates relative to the U.S. Federal Reserve as investors reassess the outlook.
That shift could weaken the euro, particularly if concerns about French public finances increase the risk premium on eurozone assets.
Citi’s foreign exchange strategists said EUR/USD could fall below 1.10 if the currency undershoots fair value implied by two-year interest rate differentials.
Its two-year valuation model suggests a 50 to 75 basis point reduction in the euro-U.S. rate spread could push EUR/USD towards 1.1075 to 1.1000, even without an additional undershoot.
Citi identified receiving ECB rates against Fed rates as its preferred trade, arguing the position could remain attractive if tensions involving Iran ease.
Lower commodity prices following an Iran resolution could support French equities, government bonds and the euro, making outright bearish positions in those assets less attractive.
Citi’s analysis suggests that fiscal uncertainty and a more accommodative ECB response could both pressure the euro, leaving the currency vulnerable to further declines as investors reassess the central bank’s policy outlook.

title: European bank stocks slide 8% as bond yields spark investor caution - Bloomberg
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher, Nasdaq and Dow post weekly gains as oil eases
Investing.com -- European banking stocks have fallen sharply over the past two weeks as rising government bond yields and mounting concerns over France’s public finances prompt investors to reassess one of the region’s strongest-performing sectors.
The Euro Stoxx Banks index has declined about 8%, reaching its lowest level since June and entering a technical correction on Thursday, according to Bloomberg.
Societe Generale, Credit Agricole and Deutsche Bank have each fallen more than 15% from their recent highs.
The selloff has been driven largely by surging sovereign bond yields, particularly in France, where political uncertainty and fiscal concerns have pushed the country’s borrowing premium over Germany to its widest in more than a decade.
Higher yields threaten to increase loan defaults, slow lending activity and reduce the value of government bonds held by banks.
"Bond yields appear to have crossed a pain threshold that has prompted investors to reassess fundamentals," said Roberto Scholtes, head of strategy at Singular Bank.
The retreat follows a three-year rally that saw European banking shares triple since 2022, leaving the sector vulnerable to profit-taking.
Bank of America’s September fund manager survey showed a net 25% of European investors were overweight banking stocks, highlighting crowded positioning.
European banking supervisors have increased scrutiny of sovereign debt exposures, which represented approximately 13% of bank assets at the end of 2025.
Regulators believe higher net interest income is largely offsetting losses on bond holdings for now.
JPMorgan strategists described the decline in French banking shares as a potential buying opportunity, assuming yields do not rise substantially further.
Morgan Stanley similarly suggested that prolonged bond market volatility would be necessary to undermine the sector’s underlying fundamentals.
Investors will now turn to third-quarter earnings reports later this month for evidence of continued lending growth and profitability.
Barclays strategists expect the results to refocus attention on banks’ financial strength after the recent market volatility.

title: Why is the Chinese stock market missing the AI rally
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher, Nasdaq and Dow post weekly gains as oil eases
Investing.com -- China’s stock market has missed the global artificial intelligence rally in 2026, as economic weakness, limited AI hardware exposure and regulatory uncertainty weigh on investor sentiment, according to Yardeni Research.
China’s CSI 300 index has fallen nearly 6% this year, contrasting with gains exceeding 65% in South Korea’s Kospi and Taiwan’s Weighted Index, Yardeni said.
The divergence follows Chinese developer Moonshot AI’s July release of a competitive low-cost model, reinforcing China’s position in the global AI race.
Yardeni identified three reasons for the underperformance.
First, China’s economy faces weak consumption, deflation, youth unemployment and a property downturn now in its fifth year.
The housing slump has eroded household wealth and reduced local government revenue from land sales, constraining economic activity.
Second, China’s major equity benchmarks lack the concentration of AI hardware manufacturers driving regional markets.
South Korea and Taiwan benefit from semiconductor suppliers Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and TSMC, which are closely tied to global AI infrastructure spending.
China’s strengths lie primarily in AI models and applications, with domestic hardware companies trading mainly outside major benchmarks.
Third, regulatory uncertainty continues to discourage investors following Beijing’s technology crackdowns, including its intervention in Alibaba affiliate Ant Group’s planned listing.
Yardeni also highlighted US-China tensions and potential American restrictions on advanced chip exports and investment.
These concerns have weighed on valuations. The MSCI China index’s forward price-to-earnings ratio has declined to 10.2 from 11.7 in mid-May.
The weakness persists even after onshore-listed companies reported nearly 26% profit growth in the second quarter, their strongest quarterly increase in five years.
Yardeni warned that China’s dependence on AI-related exports poses another risk. Nomura estimates semiconductors, computers and related products account for roughly half of China’s export growth.
A slowdown in global AI spending could hurt China’s economy, even though its broader stock market has missed the rally elsewhere in Asia.

BRUSSELS, Oct 10 (Reuters) - The European Union’s long-term budget for the period 2028 to 2034 should be 8% lower than the European Commission’s proposed €2 trillion, the Irish EU presidency said on Saturday.
This would result in a budget of €1.6 trillion, according to the Irish proposal, though it will be subject to contentious negotiations among EU countries in the coming months.
The proposal still marks a 30% increase over the current budget, which runs from 2021 to 2027, and is certain to face stiff resistance from some countries such as Germany that want to keep a firm lid on spending.
The EU budget is the main source of financing for all of the 27-country bloc’s main policies.
The Commission, the EU executive, has said the bloc will have to deal with new challenges such as spending more on defence and making Europe more competitive, while some EU countries want to retain most of the expenditure on old policies to support farming and regional development.
"The Negotiating Box provides savings of 8%, or €141 billion, on the Commission’s original proposal," said Ireland, current holder of the EU’s six-month rotating presidency, referring to its compromise proposal.
Ireland put the Commission’s original €2 trillion figure at €1.76 trillion based on 2025 prices, which resulted in an 8% reduction.
The proposal sets out a 3% cut in spending on regional development, agriculture and fisheries spending from the Commission’s own figures, and a 13% reduction in spending on competitiveness, prosperity and security.
It foresees €55 billion in new financing options derived from customs duties and selling CO2 emissions permits to companies, among other sources.
EU leaders will discuss the Irish proposal in Brussels on October 15 to 16. The EU budget, which is known as the Multiannual Financial Framework, needs to be agreed by all 27 member states.
While more frugally-minded countries such as Germany, the Netherlands and the Nordic countries have called for budget cutbacks, others including Spain, Italy and Poland are keen to protect expenditure.

title: Where could stocks and bonds collide? Here’s what to watch
full_text:

Investing.com -- U.S. stocks have historically held up well even as bond yields rise, but a prolonged increase in real Treasury yields above the economy’s underlying growth rate could eventually put pressure on equities, according to BCA Research.
In a report dated Ocober. 5, BCA Research’s chief U.S. investment strategist Doug Peta said the level of interest rates matters more for equity returns than their direction.
Real yields remain below levels that could derail the bull market, but a sustained rise above potential growth could mark a turning point. Historically, the S&P 500 returned an annualized 9.9% when real 10-year Treasury yields rose at least 100 basis points, versus 5.5% when they fell by that amount.
The index’s annualized price return across all periods since October 1948 was 8.2%, BCA’s historical analysis showed.
Why rising bond yields have not derailed stocks
Higher interest rates reduce the present value of future corporate earnings, but BCA Research said their impact on equities also depends on earnings expectations.
Rising real rates often accompany stronger economic momentum and upward earnings revisions, while falling rates can coincide with weaker earnings. The net effect depends on whether changes in earnings or valuation multiples dominate.
Unlike bonds, whose sensitivity to interest rates can be measured through duration, equities respond to numerous interacting factors.
Historical data show that the S&P 500 delivered an annualized return of 11.8% when real 10-year Treasury yields rose but remained below the economy’s potential growth rate. Returns averaged 8.6% when yields rose from below to above potential growth, and fell to negative 1.3% when yields started and ended above that threshold.
There is no single interest-rate threshold
BCA found that S&P 500 valuation multiples tend to be lower when real yields reach 5.5% or higher. Extremely low yields can support valuations but may also signal deflationary pressures.
Between 2% and 5%, multiples vary widely, limiting the usefulness of interest rates alone as a market indicator.
BCA also found no evidence of investors systematically shifting from equities into bonds when yields rise or the equity risk premium falls. Institutional allocations face regulatory and mandate constraints, while households tend to respond to recent stock-market performance.
For one-year forward returns, the direction of yields mattered less - the S&P 500’s annualized return was 7.9% following rising real yields and 8.6% following falling yields. However, returns averaged 9.6% when real yields were below potential growth and 5.9% when they were above it.
What investors should watch
BCA does not expect higher real rates to materially hurt economic activity or corporate earnings unless they exceed potential growth for several months.
It estimates long-run potential growth at roughly 2%, compared with a real 10-year Treasury yield of 1.59% in August that could approach 2% after September price data are incorporated.
The likeliest path to a stock-and-bond collision, it said, is a prolonged period of real Treasury yields above potential growth. Investors should monitor small-cap earnings and credit performance, household delinquencies, and private-equity delinquencies and restructurings.
Smaller companies are particularly vulnerable because they rely more heavily on variable-rate loans, while larger firms often access fixed-rate bond funding. Private entities have also been among the cycle’s most aggressive borrowers.

The analysts highlighted a 98% drop in cost per token since 2024, even as AI-related revenue has soared on rising enterprise volumes that BMO said are still in the early innings.
"We also expect cost-to-serve AI to continue declining meaningfully as infrastructure scales, hardware improves, and optimizations occur across the entire AI stack," they wrote, adding that expert calls suggest token prices may bottom around 2030, after which closed-source model providers may seek to raise prices.
Alphabet "remains a clear leader across the AI stack," BMO stressed, arguing that full-stack ownership will let it benefit from optimizations at every layer as AI scales. The Gemini Agent launch and Gemini 4 Argo release help offset fears that Alphabet is losing its edge in the AI race, the analysts said.
Citi names its top chip stocks ahead of Q3 earnings
Citi has named AMD, Texas Instruments, Lam Research, Teradyne and Synopsys as its top Buy-rated semiconductor picks ahead of third-quarter earnings, saying it is becoming "increasingly selective" on the sector after a sharp rebound.
Analyst Atif Malik noted the SOX index has rebounded notably from its summer correction, in line with Citi’s earlier call. The industry remains in "Phase 2" of the bank’s playbook, supported by robust data center demand — now about 40% of the semiconductor market — and a continuing recovery in auto and industrial markets at roughly 20% of demand, while PC and smartphone demand remains weak.
Estimate revision momentum slowed in the second quarter, with further moderation expected in the third. Networking, semiconductor equipment and analog chips show the strongest momentum, followed by compute and memory.
Citi expects the largest sales estimate revisions in compute, particularly networking names such as Marvell and Astera Labs and CPU-exposed names AMD, Intel and Nvidia, followed by analog names Texas Instruments and Analog Devices, then equipment makers Lam Research and Teradyne.
"While 4Q is typically a seasonally weaker quarter for analog semis, we expect most companies to guide above seasonal trends," Malik said.
Wall Street raises targets on Marvell after analyst day
Earlier this week, Wall Street analysts raised their price targets on Marvell Technology after the chipmaker laid out a much larger long-term revenue outlook at its analyst day.
Management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to about $20 billion from $18 billion and introduced a fiscal 2031 framework of $70-90 billion at the midpoint of $80 billion — roughly 10 times fiscal 2026 levels — targeting earnings above $30 per share, gross margins of 56-59% and a 2030 addressable market of about $400 billion.
TD Cowen upgraded to Buy from Hold, raising its target to $350 from $245. Analyst Sean O’Loughlin said growth drivers have "fully shifted" to Marvell’s connectivity franchise and that concentration and margin risk tied to custom chips "has been largely de-risked," with custom accelerators now about 19% of the 2030 target versus more than 40% of expectations last year.
He acknowledged TD Cowen’s downgrade a year ago was "very wrong" about connectivity, while cautioning the market is unlikely to give full credit to the targets given investor focus on risks in 2028 or earlier.
Jefferies raised its target to $450 from $325, calling $30 of 2030 EPS "conservative" with potential for $35-40 depending on mix, and said the $37.5 billion interconnect target for fiscal 2031 was "well ahead of expectations."
Separately, Stifel upped its target to $370 from $350, saying the targets are built bottom-up with "no single mega socket required," with scenario analysis putting fiscal 2031 EPS between $24.30 and $40.59.
B. Riley also raised its price objective to $365 from $315, noting the 2030 sales and earnings targets were 73% and 67% above consensus, with the model resting on more than 100 active projects.
Susquehanna raised to $340 from $265, saying opex should grow at half the pace of revenue through fiscal 2031.
Citi cuts NXP to Neutral on limited data center exposure, muted auto outlook
Citi has downgraded NXP Semiconductors to Neutral from Buy, cutting its price target to $260 from $370, saying it expects weaker earnings estimate revisions than peers heading into 2027.
Analyst Atif Malik said Citi believes the analog upturn is "more than halfway through," with further upside increasingly driven by data center buildouts, an area where NXP has limited exposure at just 3-4% of sales, the lowest among peers. By contrast, 56% of revenue is tied to the automotive market, where demand remains subdued.
Citi lowered its 2027 and 2028 EPS estimates to $16.30 and $18.64 from $16.61 and $21, now in line with the Street, on weaker auto and industrial assumptions. The new $260 target applies a 14 times P/E multiple to 2028 earnings, down from 17 times, in line with NXP’s five-year average and reflecting its lower data center exposure relative to peers.
The downgrade is part of a more selective stance on chip stocks following the SOX index’s rebound from its summer correction. Citi also downgraded Universal Display to Sell with a $71 target, citing smartphone market weakness next year, and moved Nova to Neutral with a $415 target, saying its risk-reward looks balanced.
Truist initiates IBM at Hold, stays cautious on near-term execution
Truist Securities has initiated coverage of IBM at Hold with a $240 price target, saying it is constructive on the company’s long-term position in enterprise computing but cautious on near-term execution.
Analysts led by Arvind Ramnani said IBM is positioned across four areas: the mainframes where much of the world’s transaction data resides, software that works across AI models, Red Hat, and a consulting arm that helps clients deploy AI.
The central question is timing. "When will enterprise spending on AI infrastructure translate into demand for IBM?" they asked.
Software now makes up 45% of revenue and 61% of segment pre-tax income, with about 80% of it recurring and annual recurring revenue of $24.6 billion growing 8%. The analysts called IBM’s second-quarter miss "an execution and timing issue rather than a structural problem," noting clients shifted budgets toward servers, storage and memory to secure supply-constrained AI hardware, while dozens of large mainframe-linked software contracts were deferred rather than canceled.
IBM lowered its full-year constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 4-5% from 5%-plus, sizing the software shortfall at $400-500 million.
IBM shares fell more than 20% after the miss, mostly through multiple compression, with forward P/E dropping to 16 times from 22 times. The stock now trades at about 17 times forward earnings. The analysts said three catalysts could make them more constructive: deferred contracts closing without meaningful discounts, a sustained improvement in Transaction Processing growth, and stronger organic software growth rather than acquisition-driven gains.

title: The midterm strategy driving Democrats deep into Trump country
full_text:
Wall Street ends higher, Nasdaq and Dow post weekly gains as oil eases
By Leah Douglas, Joseph Ax and Tim Reid
WASHINGTON, Oct 10 (Reuters) - On paper, Democrat Justin Pearson, a 31-year-old Tennessee state legislator, has little chance of winning the state’s 9th Congressional District, which Republican lawmakers redrew months ago from a Democratic stronghold to a deeply Republican seat.
Yet this week the national Democratic Party added the rural district to its list of midterm targets in November, part of a broader strategy to compete in President Donald Trump’s conservative heartland despite long odds of flipping it.
On its face, the strategy may look like Democratic overreach. Voters living in the 9th District’s newly reconfigured boundaries, for instance, picked Trump by more than 21 points in 2024.
More than a dozen Democratic operatives, strategists and candidates told Reuters the goal in part is to force Republicans to spend money defending safe seats, draining resources from the swing districts that will decide control of the US House.
By expanding the map, the party is also signaling to donors that races are becoming more competitive amid high prices and the Iran war driving Trump’s unpopularity, helping unlock money that might otherwise stay on the sidelines, they said.
"These expansions force Republicans to go on defense in more districts," said one House campaign official, speaking on the condition of anonymity. "It’s also a signal to donors and outside groups that House Democrats are taking these races seriously."
REPUBLICANS DISMISSIVE OF NEW MAP
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, the party’s US House campaign arm, this week added Pearson’s race and 13 others to its target list, expanding its battlefield to 66 Republican-held seats.
Getting on the target list gives candidates access to national party staff and campaign tools, while also raising their profiles with donors, potentially opening new streams of fundraising for their campaigns.
There are early signs the strategy is having some effect. Republican-aligned groups have begun spending in some newly added districts, while two Democratic campaigns in Republican districts told Reuters their fundraising accelerated after being placed on the target list.
Republicans have dismissed the idea that Democrats have a serious chance of defeating their party in districts that overwhelmingly voted for Trump in 2024.
Mike Marinella, a spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Committee - the party’s House campaign group - accused the Democratic Party of "stretching its map a mile wide and an inch deep, pretending every district in America is suddenly a battleground." He said the strategy will force Democrats to spend in long-shot contests when the party is already being outspent by Republicans.
Analysts, too, are skeptical.
"I’ll take it seriously when they actually put their money where their mouth is. There is a point at which it becomes fantasy land," said David Wasserman, an elections analyst at the nonpartisan Cook Political Report, which rates many of these races as safely Republican.
Democrats say they have chosen these districts for a number of reasons, including the quality of their candidates and the chance they might pull off upset wins to increase the size of a potential House majority.
FOLLOWING THE MONEY
It remains unclear how much money Democrats will ultimately devote to the newly added districts. Recent campaign finance filings are not yet available, and the party declined to tell Reuters where it is spending or how much it plans to spend on its expanded map.
But there are signs Republicans are paying attention. Restoration of America PAC, funded primarily by billionaire Richard Uihlein, spent nearly $750,000 on digital ads backing Republican David Flippo in Nevada’s 2nd District last week, according to Federal Election Commission filings.
The district, which Trump carried by 14 points in 2024, is among the recent additions to the Democratic target list.
"Democrats are on offense, Republicans are running scared, even in deep-red territory, and our expansive map reflects it," DCCC Chair Suzan DelBene said in a statement.
The new target list includes districts in Arkansas, New York and Virginia that Trump carried by as many as 24 points. Democrats say rising costs and dissatisfaction with some Trump policies are creating openings in rural and Republican-leaning areas.
"Rural America is unhappy with tariffs and rising fuel and farm costs, and that’s pushing us into redder areas," Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said.
Democrats will need a net gain of four to retake the House. However, only about 50 of the 435 House races are expected to be competitive.
TENNESSEE DREAMING
Tennessee Republicans in May split the heavily Democratic Memphis area into three districts, transforming the 9th from a majority-Black urban seat into a sprawling district stretching more than 200 miles (322 km) across rural western Tennessee, a change that made the seat significantly more favorable to Republicans.
Yet Pearson says he has found independent and Republican voters frustrated by the high cost of living who are open to voting Democratic.
"We’ve traveled across all 15 counties, filling churches and community centers in places people said we couldn’t compete," said Pearson, a Black lawmaker who gained national attention in 2023 when the Republican-majority legislature expelled him for joining a gun-violence protest at the state Capitol.
Republicans have portrayed Pearson as an outspoken progressive activist, pointing to his participation in gun-control and voting-rights protests.
"The people in Tennessee Nine, they have a clear choice. They can choose confidence over chaos, and they can choose common sense over communism, and they can choose a lawmaker over a troublemaker," his Republican opponent, state senator Brent Taylor, told Reuters.
There has been little public polling on the race, which Cook rates "Solid Republican."
EXCITE DONORS
Being added to the target list can quickly pay dividends for a campaign. Candidates or representatives from four Democratic campaigns on the DCCC’s list told Reuters they either expected to see a boost in donations or were already seeing an uptick since their addition.
Pearson said his campaign has seen a surge of financial support after being added to the list, which would boost his get-out-the-vote operation.
"This race is going to be tight. It’s going to be close. It’s going to come down to how many people can we see before Election Day, knocking on those doors and reaching out to them directly," he said.
But Democrats’ ambitions are constrained by a relative cash shortage.
While Democratic candidates nationally have outraised their Republican opponents, Republican national party committees and Republican-aligned super PACs have far outstripped Democratic counterparts in money raised.
Democrats in tough races in the expanded map said they are connecting with small-dollar donors by focusing on cost-of-living issues and campaigning heavily at town halls and other local appearances.

The Enterprise Chamber of the Amsterdam Court of Appeal said it found no sufficient grounds to question Philips' policies or management practices that would justify an inquiry.

RAMALLAH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
Abbas’ decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to vote.
There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead next month. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Abbas’ rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
Abbas has ruled by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009.
The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel’s continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November.
In Gaza, the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
There was no immediate Israeli comment on Abbas’ announcement, with officials unavailable for comment on Saturday, the Jewish Sabbath. Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognize.
The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process.
PLEDGE TO HOLD VOTE AFTER TWO DECADES

However, the agreement is only a first step towards addressing a trade imbalance exceeding €1 billion ($1.16 billion) a day, according to European Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič.

Germany is particularly exposed as its traditional export model, built around automobiles, machinery and capital goods, faces growing competition in China and third markets. China's share of global car exports rose from 5% in 2013 to 11% in 2023 and 15% in 2025, matching Germany's share, Deutsche Bank said.
Machinery, transport equipment, electrical machinery, green technologies and industrial intermediate goods face the greatest competitive pressure. The share of EU exports directly competing with Chinese exports has more than tripled in 30 years to about 7% of EU gross domestic product.
Including products where China's advantage may be emerging lifts exposure above 10% of GDP, more than twice the 1996 level. Europe retains advantages in selected chemicals, pharmaceuticals, precision instruments and specialised industrial niches.
The Beijing agreement could reduce Chinese hybrid and plug-in hybrid car exports to the EU by several million vehicles over four years. China also agreed to improve access for around €4 billion of EU exports and streamline licences for rare earths and permanent magnets, although implementation details remain undisclosed.
Chinese exports to the EU reached $560 billion in 2025, against $268.3 billion in European exports to China, Reuters reported, citing UN Comtrade data. Deutsche Bank said cheaper Chinese imports benefit consumers and downstream industries but risk eroding European manufacturers' margins and investment.
If concessions prove insufficient, the EU could investigate Chinese plug-in hybrid vehicles for subsidies, potentially introducing provisional tariffs in early 2027.
France and Germany have also proposed a trade-defence instrument enabling responses to disputes within 24 hours, while the Commission is developing DiversifyEU to reduce strategic supplier dependence.
Deutsche Bank said lasting competitiveness requires domestic reforms, including lower energy costs, faster permitting, better infrastructure and deeper capital markets. "They’re going to make assessments this morning, and I think that’ll give us a good sense about the future for the rapidity of the power restoration," DeSantis told a press conference in Tallahassee. Some 16,000 utility linemen had prepared to respond to the storm, he said.

Alabama’s emergency management agency said the downed trees and power lines made travel hazardous in Houston County, which is under a flash flood warning.
"Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice," it posted on X.

Meanwhile, specialised GPU infrastructure providers, known as neoclouds, have gained ground as demand for AI computing capacity exceeds supply.
CoreWeave captured approximately 2% of the $220 billion IaaS market, according to Bernstein, benefiting from demand for GPU-intensive model training.
The analysts expect neoclouds to face increasing competitive pressure as computing capacity expands and AI spending shifts towards inference.
Bernstein estimates inference spending could eventually exceed model training expenditure by five to 20 times.
Microsoft appears particularly well positioned because enterprise applications and data already reside on its platforms, making migration to alternative providers difficult.
Oracle could benefit from growing AI infrastructure demand, particularly through its relationship with OpenAI, while MongoDB stands to gain from increased database usage.
Snowflake faces greater competition as it expands into AI development platforms.
Gartner forecasts AI-optimised IaaS revenue reaching $174 billion by 2030, within a broader $662 billion infrastructure market.
Bernstein expects AI labs to become increasingly important platform competitors, while neoclouds could eventually remain smaller, specialised infrastructure providers.

“We welcome the opportunity to work with the Department of Labor and related government agencies to answer any questions they may have,” the Indian IT services company said in an exchange filing on Saturday.
The U.S. government announced the suspension on Thursday, affecting several major technology and IT services firms, including Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Cognizant, Microsoft, Adobe and Capgemini.
The affected companies will be unable to submit new PERM applications or have pending applications processed under the suspension.
The move forms part of the Trump administration’s broader crackdown on skilled foreign labour. U.S. officials have alleged that some companies used the program to replace American workers with lower-cost foreign employees.
PERM is separate from the H-1B temporary work visa program, and the suspension does not appear to directly affect existing H-1B visa holders.
